note: US cash equity/bond markets (NYSE, Nasdaq, Treasuries) are CLOSED all day today, Thu Nov 26, for Thanksgiving, reopening for a shortened 9:30am-1:00pm ET session on Black Friday Nov 27 -- so nothing in the US book is actionable until Friday's half-day or Monday. 10 of 12 items below are dated Nov 24-26 (well above the 3-5 freshness minimum); the remaining two (Nvidia SEC probe, SMIC Q3) are slightly older but kept as live, unresolved tail-risk/structural context for the HK tech sleeve. Asia/crypto/geopolitics kept moving overnight as expected: Hang Seng's Thu-morning bounce, Bitcoin's partial recovery, the Russia-Estonia escalation, and the Taiwan PLA exercise are all genuinely new since Wed's US close.

items.headline: Silver smashed to a one-year low near $39-41 as CME hikes margins (silver 8%->9%, gold 5%->6%) right as hot PCE cements a December Fed hike
items.summary: Silver futures fell 4.6-5.7% on Nov 25 to roughly $38.90-40.71, deepening a 25%+ monthly slide that Tavi Costa called the worst year-to-date performance in 30 years; CME's margin hike on gold and silver took effect after Tuesday's close, raising the cost of carrying leveraged positions just as the hot PCE print cemented ~94-97% odds of a Dec 9 Fed hike. Gold broke below $3,500 for the first time since September 2025, falling about 3% to roughly $3,446-3,476.
items.actionable: This is the most acute threat to the book right now -- a margin-hike-driven leverage squeeze stacked on a hawkish Fed repricing is exactly the scenario that pushes a silver-collateralized loan toward a margin call, so preserving cash buffer and reducing leverage takes priority over any dip-buying instinct.

items.headline: COMEX registered silver drains another 3.1M oz in a day even as price falls -- 'silver crisis' chatter builds
items.summary: Physical COMEX registered silver stocks fell by roughly 3.1 million ounces in a single session this week even as futures prices kept dropping, a divergence analysts flag as genuine physical tightness beneath paper-market liquidation. Front-month contracts for gold, silver, platinum and palladium are all trading below spot -- a backwardation signal of physical scarcity -- fueling renewed talk of a potential COMEX silver delivery squeeze, though no default has occurred.
items.actionable: The inventory/price divergence means the loan's silver collateral could see a violent short-covering snapback if physical delivery stress bites, but until that happens the price trend is still down -- don't read inventory draws alone as a buy signal while margin pressure dominates.

items.headline: October core PCE jumps to 3.3% y/y (highest in ~3 years), GDP beats -- December Fed hike now near-certain
items.summary: October core PCE rose 3.3% y/y (vs 3.2% forecast, up from 3.1%) and 0.3% m/m, while headline PCE hit 3.8% y/y; Q3 GDP's second estimate also beat forecasts. New York Fed President John Williams said policymakers have 'more work to do' on inflation, while Governor Waller continued floating a possible 50bp move; CME FedWatch and Polymarket now price a December 9 hike at roughly 94-97%.
items.actionable: The inflation read confirmed the worst case flagged in the prior preview -- real-rate pressure from a near-certain Dec 9 hike is a headwind for gold/silver and a drag on HK-tech/SGX risk appetite, reinforcing a defensive, cash-heavy stance into the holiday-thinned session.

items.headline: Hang Seng snaps six-day losing streak as Xiaomi rebounds 4% despite a 68% profit collapse
items.summary: The Hang Seng rose about 46 points to 22,265 in Thursday morning trade (Nov 26 HK time), ending a six-day losing run, led by Xiaomi's 4.1% rebound after Q3 results beat lowered expectations even as net profit plunged 68.4% (adjusted profit -56.8%) on rising memory-chip costs and a widening EV/AI segment loss -- Xiaomi's third straight quarter of revenue decline (-5.2%). Several major banks reportedly backed the stock after the print.
items.actionable: Xiaomi's 'beat on a lowered bar despite deteriorating fundamentals' pattern is the same AI-capex/margin story hitting the whole HK tech sleeve -- a bounce here is tradeable but not yet evidence the sector's underlying profitability problem is resolved.

items.headline: PLA runs unannounced 'isolation' exercise toward Guam as Taiwan heads into Nov 28 local elections under PRC interference
items.summary: US analysts assess the PLA is very likely conducting a major, unannounced military exercise simulating an extended isolation of Taiwan, with naval operations extending beyond the first island chain toward Guam -- signaling a rehearsal of blocking US/allied reinforcement in a contingency. Separately, Taiwanese prosecutors indicted a Taoyuan city-council candidate on Nov 20 for taking PRC campaign funding ahead of Taiwan's Nov 28 elections, and the Legislative Yuan passed a supplemental ~NT$145.7bn (~US$4.6bn) defense-spending budget the same day.
items.actionable: A PLA exercise rehearsing blockade of reinforcement routes to Taiwan is a standing tail risk for the SMIC/HK-tech sleeve specifically (Taiwan Strait supply-chain exposure) -- it doesn't change today's positioning but argues against adding further China-tech beta into the Nov 28 election window.

items.headline: Russia accuses Estonia of enabling Ukrainian drone strikes, warns the NATO ally is 'on the verge of triggering open war'
items.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry accused Estonia of a range of hostile actions -- including tacitly allowing Ukrainian drones to use its airspace for attacks on northwestern Russia -- and warned the situation was approaching 'open war'; NATO states deny intentionally permitting the drone transits. The escalation follows Estonia's announcement of a six-month border closure with Russia and comes alongside Ukraine's continuing deep-strike campaign against Russian energy infrastructure.
items.actionable: A direct Russia-NATO-member threat is a fresh escalation vector beyond the existing Ukraine-strikes-on-oil story -- it is one of the few live catalysts that could put a safe-haven bid under gold even while silver remains under separate margin/liquidation pressure.

items.headline: OPEC+ faces its most complicated meeting in years on Nov 29, setting 2027 quotas against a forecast 1.7mb/d Q4 supply surplus
items.summary: OPEC+ ministers meet in Vienna on Sunday Nov 29 to set 2027 production baselines, with no agreed output framework beyond December 31 and a sweeping first-ever capacity audit on the table the same day. The IEA projects global oil supply will outpace demand by 1.7 million barrels/day in Q4 2026 -- the first surplus since the US-Iran war -- while Brent has already fallen to three-month lows near $89 amid the oversupply narrative and improving US-Iran diplomacy.
items.actionable: A surprise supply-discipline signal at Sunday's meeting versus the market's current expectation of inaction is a near-term risk to the book's disinflation/stagflation assumptions underlying the Fed-hike and cash-heavy thesis -- watch for headlines over the long weekend.

items.headline: Bitcoin claws back to ~$60-61k, up 10% off Saturday's $55,130 low, even as hot PCE hardens Fed-hike bets
items.summary: Bitcoin has rebounded to roughly $60,000-61,200 as of Nov 26, about 10% above its Nov 21 low of $55,130, though the Nov 25 PCE print (core 3.3%, headline 3.8%) and near-certain December Fed hike are being cited as a fresh headwind weighing on crypto risk appetite. US spot Bitcoin ETFs had logged a record $4.71bn of November outflows through Nov 24, leaving it unclear whether the bounce reflects genuine demand or short covering.
items.actionable: Crypto's partial recovery despite a hawkish Fed repricing is a tentative sign the broader risk-rally narrative hasn't fully round-tripped, but the scale of November ETF outflows argues for treating it as unconfirmed rather than a signal to add risk elsewhere in the book.

items.headline: Lynas locks in a 10-year Malaysia license renewal and a 2038 price floor, plus a Brazil acquisition; MP Materials' NdPr output up 41%
items.summary: At its FY26 AGM, Lynas said Malaysia renewed its operating license for 10 years and detailed a 12-year JARE agreement with a US$110/kg NdPr floor price through 2038, plus new downstream deals for a Malaysian magnet factory and an agreement to acquire Brazil's Meteoric Resources (light and heavy rare earths). MP Materials separately reported Q3 NdPr separation at Mountain Pass up 41% y/y to 1,018 tonnes, sold at a realized ~$100/kg under its 10-year, $110/kg DoD price-floor contract.
items.actionable: Government-backed price floors on both the Lynas-JARE deal and the MP-DoD contract are turning the watch-list names into structurally de-risked, policy-subsidized earners rather than pure China-leverage headline trades -- this strengthens the fundamental case for adding to the rare-earth watchlist independent of the next Busan-truce headline.

items.headline: STI slips 0.6% on Seatrium retrenchment and bank weakness, but S-REITs buck the tape as T-bill yields keep falling
items.summary: The Straits Times Index fell 0.6% to 4,930.83 on Nov 25, dragged by Seatrium (-4.2% on retrenchment news) and DBS/OCBC (down 0.2-1.2%), even as Singtel rose 1.9%. Singapore REITs moved the other way -- the FTSE ST All-Share Real Estate REIT Index was up 0.61% with 21 advancers vs 9 decliners, led by industrial/logistics names, as short-term T-bill yields continue easing from their 4%+ peak.
items.actionable: REITs decoupling positively from a down STI session on falling T-bill yields is incremental confirmation of the mean-reversion thesis flagged previously -- it's a reason to hold rather than trim the S-REIT sleeve, while the bank/Seatrium weakness is a reminder the cyclical/industrial side of the SGX book still faces headwinds.

items.headline: Nvidia's SEC accounting probe widens scrutiny of the Singapore-erasing revenue-reporting change; stock fell 13% on the report
items.summary: The SEC's civil investigation into Nvidia is focused on potential investor-disclosure violations tied to its 2025 shift from billing-address to customer-headquarters revenue reporting, which removed Singapore (previously near half of global revenue under the old method) from its geographic breakdown; Nvidia shares fell about 13% when Reuters first detailed the probe. The scrutiny sits alongside a separate DOJ antitrust review of Nvidia's $12.9bn Hugging Face acquisition.
items.actionable: This remains a live, unresolved tail risk for the HK tech sleeve's AI-capex thesis (Tencent/Alibaba/Xiaomi all lean on the same Nvidia-driven demand backdrop) -- it's a reason not to chase the Hang Seng's Nvidia-sentiment bounces until the probe's scope is clarified.

items.headline: SMIC guides FY2026 revenue above $12bn and warns AI chip capacity stays tight through 2027-28
items.summary: SMIC's Q3 results beat estimates, with net profit up 123.4% y/y to $428.4m and revenue up 33.9% to $3.19bn; co-CEO Zhao Haijun now sees full-year revenue topping $12bn (+~30%) at a ~26% gross margin, with Q4 guidance of 4-6% sequential growth. Management flagged that AI-driven chip manufacturing capacity will stay extremely tight through 2027, with shortages persisting into mid-to-late 2028, while China accounted for 90.8% of Q3 revenue.
items.actionable: SMIC's multi-year tight-capacity guidance is a structural positive for the portfolio's SMIC exposure independent of today's HK-tech sentiment swings, though its 90%+ China-revenue concentration keeps it exposed to any escalation in the Taiwan Strait or export-control headlines above.
